name: Chapter 1: Introduction to Financial Statements and Their Analysis

questions.text: A firm reports assets of €950m and liabilities of €630m. During the next period it earns €65m of comprehensive income and makes net payouts of €40m. If liabilities remain unchanged, what is ending equity?

options.a: €385m, because all comprehensive income increases equity.
options.b: €295m, because cash distributions reduce reported assets twice.
options.c: €345m, as equity rises by the retained comprehensive income.
options.d: €360m, because net income adds to equity while dividends reduce it but share issues do not.
options.e: €280m, because net payouts are excluded from the equity statement.
options.f: €320m, because comprehensive income cannot change previously recognized owner claims.

questions.text:
Consider the statements.
I. A cash-flow statement reports transactions over a period.
II. The statement of changes in equity is a point-in-time snapshot.
III. A balance sheet depicts claims on assets at a particular date.
Which set is correct?

options.a: I and II only
options.b: I and III only
options.c: I only
options.d: III only
options.e: II and III only

questions.text: An equity analyst and a bond analyst study the same company. Which difference in their objectives is most consistent with the lecture?

options.a: The equity analyst emphasizes short-term invoices; the bond analyst emphasizes market share growth.
options.b: The equity analyst focuses on historic payments; the bond analyst ignores financial risk entirely.
options.c: The equity analyst focuses on tax filings; the bond analyst focuses on potential dividend growth.
options.d: The equity analyst is chiefly concerned with covenant compliance, whereas the bond analyst seeks capital appreciation and voting power.
options.e: The equity analyst emphasizes upside and stewardship; the bond analyst emphasizes default and covenants.

questions.text: A company earns €28m net income, reports €9m other comprehensive income, pays €14m dividends, repurchases €11m of shares and issues €5m of shares. What is the change in equity?

options.a: An increase of €12m
options.b: An increase of €3m
options.c: An increase of €28m
options.d: An increase of €17m
options.e: An increase of €37m

questions.text:
Consider the statements.
I. Retained earnings accumulate income less distributions since formation.
II. Every unrealized gain is included in net income before it reaches equity.
III. Contributed capital can change when a company issues new equity.
Which set is correct?

options.a: I and II only
options.b: III only
options.c: I and III only
options.d: None of I, II or III
options.e: II and III only

questions.text: A company announces that it will distribute substantially all accumulated cash as dividends, while major loans are approaching maturity. Which conflict is illustrated most directly?

options.a: Shareholders favor distributions, whereas creditors favor preservation of liable equity.
options.b: Shareholders favor lower profits, whereas creditors favor more volatile profits.
options.c: Shareholders favor higher interest, whereas creditors favor immediate equity issuance.
options.d: Shareholders favor delayed payments, whereas creditors favor retained earnings accounting.
options.e: Both shareholders and creditors generally prefer distributing all available cash as dividends before loan maturity.

questions.text: Which situation most directly explains why a business-model analysis should precede financial-ratio comparisons?

options.a: Identical accounting ratios imply identical industry economics once accounting policies are consistent.
options.b: Identical ratios can reflect different competitive positions and operating economics.
options.c: Identical accounting ratios guarantee identical exposure to substitutes, regulation and customer concentration.
options.d: Identical ratios prove that firms have the same durability of competitive advantage.
options.e: Accounting ratios already incorporate all customer and regulatory information.
options.f: Business models matter only when management refuses to disclose net income.

questions.text: A supplier of specialist components faces one dominant automobile buyer that can credibly switch suppliers. In Porter's five-forces framework, the principal pressure is:

options.a: buyer bargaining power, which can force selling-price concessions.
options.b: industry rivalry, because powerful buyers generally force the seller to pay its own suppliers earlier.
options.c: the threat of new entry, which primarily reduces the buyer's own fixed costs.
options.d: supplier bargaining power, which directly raises the buyer's selling price.
options.e: the threat of substitutes, which directly removes all industry rivalry.
options.f: buyer bargaining power, because the automaker can reduce the supplier’s margins only after acquiring equity control.

questions.text:
Consider the statements.
I. Entry barriers generally intensify the threat of entry.
II. More substitute products can restrict a firm's pricing freedom.
III. Supplier bargaining power can compress a firm's margin by increasing input prices.
Which set is correct?

options.a: I and III only
options.b: II and III only
options.c: III only
options.d: I, II and III
options.e: I and II only

questions.text: Two retailers report similar gross margins, but one has exclusive logistics technology and the other relies on generic outsourced services. Which framework most directly traces where their competitive advantage is created?

options.a: Porter’s five forces, because it compares inbound logistics and human-resource systems within each company.
options.b: A common-size balance sheet, because it measures the contribution of a proprietary logistics process to sales margins.
options.c: A residual-income identity, by equating market capitalization with retained earnings.
options.d: A balance-sheet identity, by excluding non-cash activities from enterprise value.
options.e: Porter's value chain, by separating primary activities from support activities.
options.f: A cash-flow classification, by moving supplier contracts into financing activities.

questions.text: A firm's procurement costs fall following a supplier-relationship redesign, while its marketing costs and revenue remain constant. Within the value chain, this change most directly concerns:

options.a: a financing activity that changes the firm's residual equity ownership.
options.b: a primary outbound activity affecting only the proceeds from loans.
options.c: a support activity affecting the margin earned by primary activities.
options.d: an external opportunity that must be recognized as an intangible asset.

questions.text: A pharmaceutical firm has a superior research team, while a rival regulator proposes much stricter approvals. Under SWOT, how should these two observations be classified?

options.a: External strength and internal threat
options.b: External opportunity and internal weakness
options.c: Internal opportunity and external strength
options.d: Internal weakness and external opportunity
options.e: Internal strength and external threat

questions.text:
Consider the statements.
I. Industry-wide regulatory tightening can be an external threat.
II. An efficient supply chain can be an internal strength.
III. A firm's weak governance is necessarily an external weakness.
Which set is correct?

options.a: II only
options.b: II and III only
options.c: I only
options.d: I and II only
options.e: I and III only

questions.text: A company's annual report reveals strong accounting profits, but major customers can terminate contracts without penalty. Which conclusion is most defensible?

options.a: Strong accounting earnings ensure that the firm's competitive advantage is durable.
options.b: Because credit sales are already recorded, customer concentration cannot alter the firm’s future bargaining power.
options.c: Customers with unrestricted termination clauses necessarily make the firm’s long-run profit margin more stable.
options.d: Annual profits should be replaced by the firm's tax expense for valuation.
options.e: Contract terms are irrelevant once earnings appear in the income statement.
options.f: Reported earnings alone are insufficient to judge the durability of the firm's advantage.

questions.text: A business issues shares for €80m, repurchases shares for €25m and distributes €30m in dividends. What is its net payout to shareholders?

options.a: €25m, indicating net cash distributed to shareholders.
options.b: −€55m, indicating net capital raised from shareholders.
options.c: €55m, indicating the dividends and repurchases together.
options.d: €135m, indicating the total value of equity transactions.
options.e: −€25m, indicating net capital raised from shareholders.

questions.text: Which item is most appropriately classified as other comprehensive income rather than a cash inflow from operating activities?

options.a: Cash collected from customers for inventory sold during the year.
options.b: An unrealized exchange gain recognized in profit on an operating trade receivable.
options.c: The non-cash recognition of depreciation on a factory used in ordinary operations.
options.d: A foreign-currency translation adjustment on a foreign operation.
options.e: A cash advance received from a bank under a revolving credit line.
options.f: Net proceeds from issuing new shares to outside shareholders.

questions.text:
Consider the statements.
I. A cash-flow statement explains the change in cash by operating, investing and financing flows.
II. The balance sheet and income statement describe different time dimensions.
III. An income statement necessarily reports the same number as cash from operations.
Which set is correct?

options.a: I and II only
options.b: I and III only
options.c: I, II and III
options.d: III only
options.e: None of I, II or III

questions.text: A company loses a patent monopoly, and rivals enter the market. Sales remain stable, but the firm sharply increases discounts. Which mechanism best explains the resulting pressure on profitability?

options.a: Increased equity financing directly forces the company to lower list prices.
options.b: Lower supplier bargaining power automatically raises the firm's cost of goods sold.
options.c: Weaker entry barriers and rivalry constrain the firm's achievable selling prices.
options.d: Greater accounting documentation immediately reduces the company's sales volume.

questions.text: In a business investment framework, investors buy newly issued bonds directly from a firm and later sell them to other investors. Which transaction provides funds directly to the issuer?

options.a: The initial issue and secondary resale each supply identical new operating cash to the issuer.
options.b: Neither trade, because debt contracts never finance operations.
options.c: The initial bond issue, not the later secondary-market resale.
options.d: Both trades, because every investor exchange increases firm cash.
options.e: Both the initial issuance and the secondary sale, but only if the secondary buyer is a financial institution.
options.f: The secondary-market resale, not the firm's original bond issue.

questions.text: A business has a material technological capability developed internally that is hard to value and mostly absent from its balance sheet. What is the key implication for financial statement analysis?

options.a: The missing capability must have zero economic value because it lacks a carrying amount.
options.b: The balance-sheet identity becomes invalid because accounting misses economic knowledge.
options.c: A qualitative assessment can reveal value drivers not fully captured by accounting recognition.
options.d: All internally generated know-how appears automatically in the shareholders' equity statement.

questions.text:
Consider the statements.
I. Debt investors can use financial information to estimate covenant-violation risk.
II. Customers have no relevant reason to evaluate supplier solvency.
III. Employees can use financial information to assess employment security.
Which set is correct?

options.a: III only
options.b: I and III only
options.c: I and II only
options.d: I, II and III
options.e: II and III only

questions.text: A competitor introduces a product that performs the same function at half the price. Which of Porter's five forces is most directly strengthened?

options.a: The firm's procurement intensity
options.b: Customer switching penalties
options.c: Threat of substitution
options.d: Supplier bargaining power

questions.text: Which assertion best distinguishes financial statement analysis from business valuation?

options.a: Analysis derives stock exchange prices from transaction volume; valuation assesses whether revenues were audited.
options.b: Analysis focuses on financing decisions alone, whereas valuation is the preparation of IFRS-conforming statements.
options.c: Analysis sets a stock's trading price; valuation prepares the audited statement of changes in equity.
options.d: Analysis is limited to investors; valuation is limited to managers and tax authorities.
options.e: Analysis extracts information on performance and financial condition; valuation estimates economic worth.
options.f: Analysis measures only cash receipts; valuation measures only current accounting assets.

questions.text: A company has opening equity of €210m, net income of €25m, OCI losses of €7m and net payouts of €12m. If no other equity transactions occur, ending equity equals:
Which of the following is the most informative response to a sharp rise in the cash ratio of a struggling manufacturer?

options.a: Determine whether cash is operationally needed or reflects financing and postponed investment.
options.b: Treat the higher cash ratio as conclusive proof of stronger long-term competitiveness.
options.c: Assume every euro of cash is excess cash available to distribute immediately.
options.d: Classify the additional cash automatically as reported current-period operating profit.

questions.text:
Consider the statements.
I. Financial statements help determine taxable profit and distributions.
II. Creditors are protected only through information on dividends already paid.
III. Documentation supports accountability for the fiscal year.
Which set is correct?

options.a: I and III only
options.b: II and III only
options.c: I and II only
options.d: None of I, II or III
options.e: I, II and III

questions.text: A firm has cash from operations of €90m, investing cash flow of −€120m and financing cash flow of €45m. Which statement describes the cash-flow result?

options.a: Cash decreases by €30m because financing is excluded from cash changes.
options.b: Cash decreases by €15m because investing outflows exceed operating inflows.
options.c: Cash increases by €135m because financing proceeds are treated as income.
options.d: Cash increases by €15m despite investing outflows exceeding operating inflows.
options.e: Cash falls by €75m because only investing and financing flows contribute to net cash changes.

questions.text: An analyst classifies a competitor's new distribution network as an external threat, but the focal firm's proprietary training program as an internal strength. Which analytical point is illustrated?

options.a: The SWOT distinction depends on whether a factor belongs to the firm or its environment.
options.b: All technology-related changes must be classified as opportunities, regardless of ownership.
options.c: Positive and negative SWOT categories are determined only from recent financial results.
options.d: A competitive advantage can be assessed without considering the external environment.

questions.text:
Consider the statements.
I. A stronger competitive advantage can arise from proprietary knowledge absent from the balance sheet.
II. A financial statement analysis cannot evaluate debt risk.
III. A firm's financial statements necessarily measure every economic asset at market value.
Which set is correct?

options.a: III only
options.b: II only
options.c: None of I, II or III
options.d: I and III only
options.e: II and III only

questions.text:
Consider the statements.
I. Customer bargaining power can constrain selling prices.
II. Supplier bargaining power can increase production costs.
III. Competitive rivalry can reduce achievable profit margins.
Which set is correct?

options.a: II and III only
options.b: I and III only
options.c: I and II only
options.d: I, II and III
options.e: I only
